heading.en: Why does a flute play only certain notes?
heading.kn: ಕೊಳಲು ಕೆಲವು ಸ್ವರಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಏಕೆ ನುಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ?

hook.en: Blow across a bottle and you get one clear note. Add water and the note rises. *Waves* bouncing back and forth inside fit only certain wavelengths.
hook.kn: ಬಾಟಲಿಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಊದಿದರೆ ಒಂದು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟ ಸ್ವರ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ. ನೀರು ಸೇರಿಸಿದರೆ ಸ್ವರ ಏರುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಳಗೆ ಹಿಂದೆ ಮುಂದೆ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಿಸುವ ತರಂಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಕೆಲವು ತರಂಗದೂರಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: Blow across a bottle and you get one clear note. Add water and the note rises. Waves bouncing back and forth inside fit only certain wavelengths. In this lesson: State the principle of superposition.
Describe reflection at rigid and open boundaries.
Find normal modes of strings and pipes.

body.en: When two or more *waves* overlap, the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements: y = y₁ + y₂. In phase they add (constructive interference); out of phase by π they cancel (destructive). A wave reflected from a rigid boundary returns with a phase change of π (a crest returns as a trough). At an open boundary it reflects with no phase change.
body.kn: ತರಂಗಗಳು ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಿಸಿದಾಗ ಫಲಿತ ಸ್ಥಾನಪಲ್ಲಟ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಸ್ಥಾನಪಲ್ಲಟಗಳ ಬೀಜಗಣಿತ ಮೊತ್ತ. ದೃಢ ಗಡಿಯಿಂದ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲನದಲ್ಲಿ π ಹಂತ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ; ತೆರೆದ ಗಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಇಲ್ಲ.

title.en: Standing waves on strings and in pipes

say.en: Two pulses meet on a string. Where they overlap, their displacements simply add: the principle of superposition.
A wave and its reflection travelling the opposite way form a standing wave. Some points never move: nodes. Halfway between are antinodes.
A string fixed at both ends must have nodes at both ends. So a whole number of half-wavelengths fit: L = n lambda over 2.
A pipe closed at one end has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. Only odd harmonics occur. An open pipe has all harmonics.
A string 0.5 metre long with wave speed 200 metres per second: fundamental 200 hertz, then 400, 600. A closed pipe 0.25 metre long in air at 340: 340 hertz, then 1020.

narration.en: Waves reflected from the two fixed ends add up to a standing wave with nodes at the ends. Only whole numbers of half wavelengths fit: λ = 2L/n, so f = n v/(2L) with v = √(T/μ). n = 1 is the fundamental; higher n are the harmonics. The string is drawn slowed down.
narration.kn: ಎರಡು ಸ್ಥಿರ ತುದಿಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಿತ ತರಂಗಗಳು ಕೂಡಿ ತುದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಸ್ಪಂದ ಬಿಂದುಗಳಿರುವ ನಿಂತ ತರಂಗ ಆಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಪೂರ್ಣ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಅರ್ಧ ತರಂಗದೂರಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೊಂದುತ್ತವೆ: λ = 2L/n, ಹಾಗಾಗಿ f = n v/(2L), v = √(T/μ). n = 1 ಮೂಲ ಸ್ವರ; ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ n ಹಾರ್ಮೋನಿಕ್‌ಗಳು. ದಾರವನ್ನು ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಚಿತ್ರಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ.

tryThis.en: Turn on the two travelling waves. Do they really add up to the standing wave?

body.en: A wave and its reflection travelling in opposite directions make a *standing* wave, with nodes (zero displacement) and antinodes (maximum), each λ/2 apart; a node and the next antinode are λ/4 apart. A string fixed at both ends has nodes at both ends: ν = n v/(2L), n = 1, 2, 3… A pipe closed at one end has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end: ν = (2n − 1) v/(4L), odd harmonics only. A pipe open at both ends: ν = n v/(2L), all harmonics.
body.kn: ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಎರಡು ತರಂಗಗಳು ನಿಂತ ತರಂಗ ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ: ನಿಸ್ಪಂದ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಸ್ಪಂದ ಬಿಂದುಗಳು λ/2 ಅಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ. ಎರಡೂ ತುದಿ ಬಿಗಿದ ತಂತಿ ಮತ್ತು ತೆರೆದ ಕೊಳವೆ: ν = nv/(2L). ಒಂದು ತುದಿ ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕೊಳವೆ: ಬೆಸ ಸಂನಾದಿಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರ, ν = (2n − 1)v/(4L).

say.en: A wave and its reflection travelling in opposite directions make a standing wave, with nodes zero displacement and antinodes maximum, each lambda /2 apart; a node and the next antinode are lambda /4 apart. A string fixed at both ends has nodes at both ends: nu equals n v over 2L, n equals 1, 2, 3... A pipe closed at one end has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end: nu equals 2n minus 1 v over 4L, odd harmonics only. A pipe open at both ends: nu equals n v over 2L, all harmonics. Node-node equals lambda /2; node-antinode equals lambda /4.
say.kn: ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಎರಡು ತರಂಗಗಳು ನಿಂತ ತರಂಗ ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ: ನಿಸ್ಪಂದ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಸ್ಪಂದ ಬಿಂದುಗಳು lambda /2 ಅಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ. ಎರಡೂ ತುದಿ ಬಿಗಿದ ತಂತಿ ಮತ್ತು ತೆರೆದ ಕೊಳವೆ: nu equals nv over 2L. ಒಂದು ತುದಿ ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕೊಳವೆ: ಬೆಸ ಸಂನಾದಿಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರ, nu equals 2n minus 1v over 4L.

say.en: String divided by open pipe: nu equals nv over 2L.
Closed pipe: nu equals 2n minus 1v over 4L, odd harmonics.

aim.en: To study how the frequency of a vibrating string depends on its length, tension and thickness. Try this: Halve the vibrating length and check that the frequency doubles; then quadruple the tension and see it double again.
aim.kn: ಕಂಪಿಸುವ ದಾರದ ಆವರ್ತನ ಅದರ ಉದ್ದ, ತುಯ್ತ ಮತ್ತು ದಪ್ಪದ ಮೇಲೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಅಧ್ಯಯನ ಮಾಡುವುದು. ಇದನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ: ಕಂಪಿಸುವ ಉದ್ದವನ್ನು ಅರ್ಧಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಆವರ್ತನ ದ್ವಿಗುಣವಾಗುವುದನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ; ನಂತರ ತುಯ್ತವನ್ನು ನಾಲ್ಕು ಪಟ್ಟು ಮಾಡಿ ಅದು ಮತ್ತೆ ದ್ವಿಗುಣವಾಗುವುದನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ.

aim.en: To find the speed of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube with two resonance positions, and the end correction. Try this: Find the two resonance lengths l₁ and l₂ and use v = 2f(l₂ − l₁): the end correction cancels out.

problem.en: A string 1 m long, fixed at both ends, carries waves at 200 m s⁻¹. Find its fundamental frequency and second harmonic.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A string 1 m long, fixed at both ends, carries waves at 200 m s⁻¹. Find its fundamental frequency and second harmonic.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A string 1 metre long, fixed at both ends, carries waves at 200 metres s to the power minus 1. Find its fundamental frequency and second harmonic.
nu 1 equals v over 2L equals 200 over 2 equals 100 hertz.
nu 2 equals 2nu 1 equals 200 hertz.
So the answer is 100 hertz and 200 hertz.

problem.en: A pipe 0.5 m long is closed at one end. Find its two lowest resonant frequencies. (v = 340 m s⁻¹)

steps.en: Only odd harmonics: next is 3ν₁ = 510 Hz.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A pipe 0.5 m long is closed at one end. Find its two lowest resonant frequencies. (v = 340 m s⁻¹)

say.en: Let us solve this together. A pipe 0.5 metres long is closed at one end. Find its two lowest resonant frequencies. (v equals 340 metres s to the power minus 1).
Fundamental: nu 1 equals v over 4L equals 340 over 2 equals 170 hertz.
Only odd harmonics: next is 3nu 1 equals 510 hertz.
So the answer is 170 hertz and 510 hertz.
